summary: workbench/tools_registry.py: the one numbered list of tools Kas may use (22 entries: the Kernel reads as one family; files read, write new, write revision, rename, move, new folder; calculation recheck; sheet set; desk acts as two families; windows observe/activate/minimise/close; apps.open; machine.state; named slots for K5 office.read/office.edit, K6 sandbox.run, K7 accessibility.read, K8 network.fetch), each with words, Kernel operation(s) or callable, arguments with where each may come from (the model alone never for a change), preconditions, effects, undo class (read/navigate/change/send) and how undone, the grant it needs, how its effect is verified, and availability with the reason. Observation receipts are a record kind in the Kernel (tool_receipts, graphite.receipt/1, append-only with digests): tool, object, revision, place, complete/partial, observed/inferred/unavailable, and status; dispatched and verified are always two receipts, the second following the first. K1 steps write their receipts in the same transaction as their journal rows (SENT->dispatched, DONE/FOUND_DONE/STILL_DONE->verified, NOT_VERIFIED, REFUSED, CHANGED_SINCE), the registry checks widen assignments.CHECKS, step preconditions block before anything is sent, and file writes are held under S1 sleep_held. New Kernel operations: tools.list, tools.receipts, windows.observe (reads), tools.use, windows.activate, windows.minimise (execute), windows.close (approve).

decisions: Families instead of one entry per operation: number 1 is every registered Kernel read (447 here, her own controls left out), 10 and 11 the desk acts that navigate or change; the member is named by operation or act. Numbers are explicit and stable; slots keep theirs.

files.write is two tools (3 new file, 4 new revision) over the one Kernel operation; they differ by precondition. A plan step may name its registry tool (new optional step key tool_key, part of the plan digest only when given); without it, files.write gets the preconditions true of both, plus the revision check when the path origin is a RECORD of that file at a revision.

The model alone may be the basis only of a read, or of moving what Graphite's own window shows (desk.navigate, as 0.8.7's table); never a change, a move of the owner's program windows (windows.activate/minimise take a grant) or a send. tools.use refuses a send outright (it goes through its own door with the owner's press).

Window actions became Kernel operations so they can be steps and pass K3's grant: activate/minimise execute, close approve (authorised only by name). windows.observe is a read whose receipts are computed but not kept (the strip and the window read it often); receipts are kept when the look is part of her work (a step or tools.use).

What a title means is an inference: a window whose title reads like a Save changes? prompt or an error gives an inferred receipt (complete false) saying what it rests on and that its text and buttons were not read; K7 can set tools_registry.ACCESSIBILITY to read inside.

apps.open is verified only when a window of the program appears (by process, else by program name, then partial); with no window list, a running process gives a partial receipt; after an interruption it is never repeated by itself (opening twice opens two). machine.state and window looks are of their moment and never re-checked on resume.
A receipt that cannot be written never undoes K1's journal row (the hook is wrapped); times are whole ms; no floating point in receipts.

release_note: Her tools, listed and checked (K2). Every tool Kasandra may use is in one numbered list: what it does, where each of its inputs may come from, what must hold first, what it changes and how that is undone, the grant it needs, and how its effect is verified. Every observation is kept as a receipt naming the tool, the file or window, the revision, the place, and whether it was complete, observed or only inferred. "Sent" and "verified" are two different receipts: saving a note is done only when the new revision's digest is on disk, and a dialog that looks like "Save changes?" is marked as an inference until it is read.
